    {Input Output : Type*} [Fintype Input] [Fintype Output]
    (actual reference : FiniteLaw Input) (channel : FiniteKernel Input Output)

    finiteKL (channel.predictive actual) (channel.predictive reference) ≤
      finiteKL actual reference

exact_semantic_metadata.invariant: Passing finite actual and reference laws through the same finite channel cannot increase finite KL when every atom carrying nonzero actual mass has strictly positive reference mass. Shared-zero atoms and zero channel entries are permitted.
exact_semantic_metadata.assumption_review: The selected primary exposes relative input support explicitly; it does not assume strict positivity of either full input law or all channel entries. Local discrete measurable instances bridge the existing finite-law theorem. This is the project's totalized real finiteKL convention under relative support, not a theorem identifying a singular native extended KL with a finite real value. The retained former primary still provides its exact full-support specialization and unchanged API.
exact_semantic_metadata.non_vacuity: Unequal full-support laws exercise the positive-support specialization. A point mass compared with a diagonal reference law has genuine shared-zero atoms and passes a deterministic projection through the relative-support theorem. Identity preserves finite KL and complete coarsening contracts it. Disjoint point masses violate the support premise: their totalized finiteKL is one while native extended KL is infinite.

    (source : FiniteLaw Source) (distortion : Source → Code → ℝ)
    (budget multiplier : ℝ) (hdistortion : ∀ x y, 0 ≤ distortion x y)
    (hmultiplier : 0 ≤ multiplier) (joint : FiniteLaw (Source × Code))

    rateDistortionDualValue source distortion budget multiplier ≤ mutualInformation joint

exact_semantic_metadata.invariant: The actual finite rate-distortion Lagrangian-infimum dual value is at most the mutual information of every joint law with the required source marginal and distortion budget, for nonnegative distortion and multiplier. The former component-bound Lagrangian inequality remains an unchanged supporting API.
exact_semantic_metadata.assumption_review: The selected primary assumes an actual feasible finite joint and nonnegative distortion and multiplier; it does not assume separately certified component lower bounds. The underlying infimum is genuinely derived. Retained support separately provides primal minimizer attainment by compactness. The reviewed finite F07 capability proves primal minimum equals nonnegative-multiplier dual supremum for every feasible finite problem, and finite dual attainment with complementary slackness under strict Slater feasibility. Those scoped capabilities do not turn this primary weak bound into unrestricted general strong duality, finite boundary dual attainment, or optimizer uniqueness. The structural-proxy disposition remains unchanged pending explicit review.
exact_semantic_metadata.non_vacuity: A feasible fair Boolean quarter-budget joint has positive mutual information and exercises the weak bound at a positive multiplier; this does not assert that the chosen multiplier maximizes the dual. Zero multiplier is a separate boundary with zero dual value on a nonempty code alphabet. Negative budgets are infeasible for nonnegative distortion; zero budget forces a unique Boolean diagonal joint while half budget has distinct information minimizers.
